newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas continues weaker, Q1 sees biggest losses.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas continues weaker, Q1 sees biggest losses.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices continued to fall on Monday as prices in the first quarter next year led the way down, traders and brokers said.

Q1 98 had seen weakness on Friday but slipped further on Monday, dealers said. After closing on Friday with bids at 16.10 pence and offers at 16.30 pence, it slipped consistently over the course of Monday. Early trades were done as high as 16.10 pence as part of a spread, before breaching the 16.00 pence level and continuing down.

A pair of deals done at 15.75 pence a therm had been seen by many as the lowest of the day, with bids then reported up to 15.80 pence against offers at 15.90 pence. But a trader reported doing a deal at 15.60 pence after that, with the closing bid/offer spread seen reasonably wide.

There were several theories to explain the continued weakness. One trader cited the fact that the Morecambe Bay fields were said not to be going into maintenance over the summer, leading to an unexpected surplus of gas some of which may end up on the spot market.
And the twin factors of J-Block gas coming onto the market as well as the Transco tender for storage gas are still cited by dealers as bearish factors on the market.

One company which had sold large volumes of Q3 gas on Friday and claimed responsibility for the weakness which pushed forward into other quarters said the experience had showed how little depth there is to the market at present.
A trader for the company added that although prices appear to have stabilised at the new lower levels, "it's still looking shaky," and he added that prices may have further to fall.

Although no deals have yet been seen starting with an eight, a trade was seen in August at 9.00 pence a therm and many are now saying that within a short time, possibly as soon as Tuesday, trades will be done below 9.00 pence a therm in some summer periods.
The first quarter next year was the most actively traded period of the day, but all summer months, the third quarter, the gas year in both 1997 and 1998, and Q2 98 were also done.
Another index trade was also seen, with a deal done for 100,000 th/d for two years from October at the average of two indices with no premium or discount.

The flexibility mechanism saw a system sell on Sunday, with 44,409,488 kWh sold in 5 lots at a SAP of 0.3057 p/kWh (around 8.96 p/th), and an SMP of 0.3004 p/kWh (around 8.80 p/th). The 7 day rolling average was 0.3639 p/kWh (around 10.66 p/th) after these sales.

The IPE futures contract saw prices slip in July and August, with trade done at 9.25 p/th in each month and at 9.275 p/th in August. But only 55 lots were done and the volumes remained thin in comparison with the spot market.
